implementation_statement: POL-02 Access Control Policy (P06) was approved 2026-08-31. Supporting procedures, including SEC-10 Information Protection for Part 37 security-related information, are due 2026-11-30.

Accounts are created in the identity provider from HR onboarding tickets and federated to SYS-01, SYS-03, SYS-04, and SYS-05. Gaps: terminations are not tied to same-day removal (one Part 37 approved individual was removed after 12 working days), and there is no quarterly access review.
evidence: IdP user export; HR termination records

implementation_statement: SaaS applications enforce role-based access. Gap: the Part 37 security plan, implementing procedures, and approved-individuals list are in a SYS-01 folder readable by 23 users; background investigation scans are readable by the payroll clerk. Restricted libraries are due 2026-09-30.
The site firewall separates the business network from the OT VLAN. Gaps: the historian is dual-homed, which bypasses the firewall, and the PACS server and NVR share the business VLAN.

Standard users have no local admin rights. Gaps: 9 users without need to know can open security-related information; 2 approved individuals no longer need vault access; backup administration is not separated from production administration.
evidence: Endpoint policy; folder export; cloud IAM export

implementation_statement: The identity provider locks accounts for 15 minutes after 10 failed attempts.
Screen lock after 10 minutes is enforced on laptops, desktops, and tablets by device management.
SYS-03 and SYS-04 end idle sessions after 30 minutes; the identity provider limits session lifetime to 12 hours.

Staff remote access uses SaaS through the identity provider with MFA; there is no staff VPN. Gap: the MSP remote management tool has unrestricted access to all office endpoints. (The OT vendor appliance is outside the boundary; see P03 G-074.)
Staff Wi-Fi uses enterprise authentication through the identity provider; guest Wi-Fi is internet-only and isolated.
Laptops, tablets, and truck tablets are enrolled in device management with encryption, screen lock, and remote wipe.
POL-05 prohibits company data on personal devices and personal cloud accounts; conditional access blocks unmanaged devices from SYS-01.
Awareness and training rules are in POL-05 (P06), approved 2026-08-31.
Annual security awareness training for all staff. Gaps: no phishing exercises, and no content on handling Part 37 security-related information or on cyber indicators at the security systems.
Role-based training planned for approved individuals (information protection and cyber indicators) and for maintenance and IT staff (OT security), starting 2026-11.

implementation_statement: SaaS, identity, and cloud audit events are generated by default. Gap: firewall, PACS server, and NVR events are not defined or collected.
SYS-01 and SYS-03 audit records include user, object, action, timestamp, and source address.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: Gap: no audit log review. Planned: monthly review of access to the Part 37 and background investigation libraries by the RSO, and weekly identity provider sign-in and firewall log review by the IT Manager, starting 2026-10.
Audit logs in SaaS and the cloud tenant cannot be altered by company users; access to the cloud audit log is limited to the 2 administrators.
Gap: identity provider and cloud logs use default retention (30 to 90 days). Planned: 1-year log workspace.
Audit record generation is enabled by default in the SaaS applications and the cloud tenant.
A control assessment was performed 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-07 (P07).
Exchanges with SYS-11 and SYS-12 are documented in section 8 of this plan. Gap: the connections to the historian, PACS, NVR, and alarm communicator are not documented or approved.
Planned: quarterly review of the POA&M and key metrics by the General Manager and RSO, starting 2026-Q4.
A standard image exists for laptops and desktops. Gap: no documented baseline for the firewall, switches, PACS server, NVR, or cloud workloads.
Endpoint settings are enforced by device management. Gaps: cloud workload hardening is not documented; 5 cameras kept default passwords.
Unused services are disabled on the standard image. Gap: the PACS server and NVR run vendor images that were never hardened.
Endpoint inventory is kept in device management. Gap: network devices, the PACS server, NVR, and cameras are not inventoried.
Contingency planning policy due 2026-12-31.
Gap: no contingency plan. The BIA (P05) was completed 2026-08-31 to drive the plan, due 2026-12-31, including hurricane steps and paper receiving forms.
Gap: backups have never been restore-tested. The first test, including Part 37 records, is scheduled for 2026-10-15.
SaaS vendors back up their applications. Cloud workloads are backed up daily. Gap: the backup vault is in the same account and region as production and is not immutable.
Recovery procedures will be documented in the contingency plan due 2026-12-31.
All users authenticate with unique accounts through the identity provider.
MFA is required for all privileged accounts; the 2 cloud administrators use hardware security keys.

Password length and banned-password list are enforced by the identity provider. Gaps: 5 IP cameras on the business network kept default admin passwords; the PACS and NVR administrator passwords are shared by 3 people.
POL-03 Incident Response Policy approved 2026-08-31 (P06).

Planned: incident log in the IT ticketing system with a security category shared with the RSO.
Notification duties are in the P08 matrix. Gap: procedures SEC-05 and TR-06 name the NRC Operations Center instead of the Florida Bureau of Radiation Control, and cyber indicators are not defined.
The incident response plan is POL-03 plus the P08 runbook.
The MSP maintains office endpoints remotely with MFA on its tool. Gap: no session logging review or restriction to named technicians.
Media and information handling rules are in POL-04 (P06).
The printed security plan is kept in the RSO's locked cabinet. Gap: electronic copies sync to 11 laptops and are not labeled.
Drives are destroyed by a certified vendor with certificates of destruction.
The PACS enforces the approved-individuals list at the vault and the server closet. Gap: badge removal is not tied to HR terminations.
The server and network closet is badge-controlled; the vault is a Part 37 security zone.

implementation_statement: Risk management strategy and acceptance levels are in POL-01 and P01. Gap: first formal cybersecurity risk assessment.
Personnel security procedures exist for Part 37 (AAP-01). Company-wide procedures are due 2026-12-31.
Part 37 background investigations with FBI fingerprint checks for the 14 approved individuals; standard background checks for other hires.
HR emails IT at termination. Gap: no same-day disable or Part 37 list and badge removal trigger.
Sanctions are in the employee handbook and POL-01 section 4.7.
Risk assessment policy is in POL-01 section 4.
The BORP is categorized Moderate (section 6 of this SSP).
Risk assessment completed 2026-07-24 with SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01). Annual update scheduled.
Gap: no vulnerability scanning. MSP to begin monthly authenticated scans of the business network, including the PACS server and NVR, 2026-11.
Risk responses are recorded in P01 and tracked in the P07 POA&M.
Critical processes and components are identified in the BIA (P05).
Security terms are in the MSP and waste tracking SaaS contracts. Gap: no standard security terms for other vendors, including the security system vendor.
The waste tracking vendor's SOC 2 Type 2 report was reviewed in P09. Gap: no reviews of the MSP, security system vendor, or predictive maintenance vendor.
Next-generation firewall at the site edge; no inbound services exposed. Gaps: flat business network that includes the PACS server, NVR, and cameras; dual-homed historian.
TLS 1.2 or higher for all SaaS and the cloud tenant; files shared with customers through the portal, not email attachments.
Providers use FIPS-validated cryptographic modules per their SOC 2 system descriptions.
SaaS and cloud storage are encrypted at rest by providers; all laptops and desktops use full-disk encryption.
Endpoint OS patches install automatically. Gaps: firewall, PACS server, NVR, and camera firmware are not patched on a schedule.
EDR on office laptops and desktops, monitored by the MSP. Gap: no malware protection on the PACS server and NVR (vendor-supported images).
EDR alerts are monitored 24x7 by the MSP. Gap: no network or log monitoring.
SaaS integrity controls are inherited. Gap: the source inventory database has no audit trail for edits and no second-person verification.
Part 37 retention periods are written into the program procedures. Gap: shipment coordination records have no retention rule.
